Subject: Order Form redline — invoice cadence, min commit phasing, and tax evidence (attached)

Mateo / team,

Thanks for sending the most recent order form. I attached our redline (ACME_OrderForm_Redline_v3.docx) with comments — the primary items our finance and procurement teams need clarified before we can issue a PO: 

- Invoice cadence and allocation: we need to understand whether Redwood will issue a single invoice to Acme Corp (US entity) or split invoices between Acme US and Acme EU when EU usage hits thresholds. Our accounting policy requires entity-level invoices unless otherwise agreed.
- Minimum commit phasing: our FP&A asks for clearer milestone triggers for the 1st tranche (we prefer a 50/25/25 schedule but need how that maps to activation vs calendar months).
- Net terms: Acme expects Net-45. Your order form still references Net-30 in a couple places — please confirm.
- Tax / withholding: our tax team needs Redwood's residency evidence and confirmation whether Redwood will gross-up for any withholding or if Acme should withhold (we can provide a W-8/W-9 as needed).

Please confirm these items and let us know if you can provide a tax residency cert (or W-9) for the invoicing entity. Also included one example invoice template (for reference) in the redline comments.

Next steps: can we target EOD Fri 5/5 to finalize the billing appendix so our procurement can cut a PO next week?

Attachments: ACME_OrderForm_Redline_v3.docx (docx)

Thanks,
Judy Park
Head of Procurement — Acme Corp

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Order Form redline — invoice cadence, min commit phasing, and tax evidence (attached)

Judy — thanks for the clear redline and the ask list. TL;DR: we can accommodate a phased invoice orchestration and provide most tax evidence; a couple small legal tweaks needed on gross-up/withholding. Summary below and next steps.

1) Invoice allocation: we can issue invoices per entity if you provide the legal entity mapping and PO numbers. Operationally we prefer a primary invoice to Acme US for any US-billed usage and separate invoices for EU-registered entities once EU usage is billed to that entity. If you confirm the entity list (and AR emails) we will update the billing appendix.

2) Proposed payment schedule (proposal):
   - 50% upfront credit applied at activation (invoice issued upon activation)
   - 25% milestone invoice at the start of month 3
   - Remaining 25% invoiced monthly in arrears over months 4–6 (or pro-rated if usage ramps slower)
   This maps to your 50/25/25 ask but keeps monthly visibility for the tail. If you prefer fixed tranches instead of monthly tailing, we can do 50/25/25 by calendar month.

3) Net terms: we are generally set up for Net-45 on enterprise orders. We will confirm the order form language to remove any stray Net-30 references.

4) Tax & withholding: we can provide a US W-9 and a Redwood tax residency statement for the billing entity (attached: Tax_Residency_Cert_ACME.pdf — sample). On gross-up: our legal team prefers to avoid unconditional gross-up obligations. Proposed approach: Acme will withhold where legally required; Redwood will provide certificates to reduce withholding where available. If Acme requires full gross-up, that will need to be negotiated in the commercial appendix.

Next steps / ask from you: please confirm the preferred split (single vs entity-split) and provide the PO number(s) and entity AR contacts. We will circulate a fresh redline with the payment cadence and updated tax clauses by EOD tomorrow after internal legal review.

Doc/links: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-link-orderform 
Attachments: (we will upload an updated redline once internal review completes)

Best,
Mateo Alvarez

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-05-04T13:18:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: Acme order form — legal redline notes (billing & tax)

Team — quick internal notes from legal on Judy's redline. Forward a cleaned set to Judy once we agree on the payment cadence. Key recommended edits: 

- Payment schedule language: change "invoice upon activation" to "invoice upon activation and monthly thereafter in arrears" to align with our standard ops. That preserves the 50% upfront credit but avoids ambiguous milestone language.
- Minimum commit proration: add explicit proration example clause (calculate based on daily usage in first 30 days) to avoid disputes if they ramp slower.
- Withholding / gross-up: we should avoid blanket gross-up. Add a two-paragraph clause: (1) Acme may withhold taxes as required by law; (2) Redwood will provide applicable residency certificates and cooperate to reduce withholding; (3) if the parties agree to a gross-up, commercial team must capture it as a one-time adjustment in the order form.
- VAT handling for EU entity: require Acme to accept tax invoice copies within 15 days of issuance; Redwood will provide VAT evidence where available.

Accounting question for Karthik: can Finance accept Net-45 for this structure (50/25/25 with monthly tail)? If not, we need to flag for revenue team and propose Net-30 + a small early-payment discount. Q to Karthik: please advise within 4 hours if Net-45 is a blocker.

I will prepare a redline that folds Judy's comments plus our recommended language. 

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts — Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai
